amendments.rule: Where a ketiv/qere unit's decision leaves the projection carrying a reading the ASV **excludes**, English that answers to the missing source word is `added`, and the note must carry the unit id, the readings that remained, and why the fallback dropped the word. The packet marks such a unit `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` beneath its variant line; an underdetermined unit whose qere fallback is still among the readings the English permits carries no such mark and is not this case. The reverse, where the retained reading is the longer one, makes the surplus tokens their own `unrepresented` unit and owes the same note. No Hebrew chapter has yet produced either — the ketiv and its qere are usually the same word differently written, so the two rarely differ in token count — and the rule stands so that the first one is recorded rather than explained away as a free English supply. Do not fold such a word onto a neighbouring token as a helper: the word that would have licensed it is not in the projection. This is `nt-greek-verse-v61` rule 97 holding for a ketiv/qere pair, and PHP.3.12 and JHN.9.28 are what it looks like when it happens. **But every sentence above governs a slot the packet has marked, and no other.** Where the ASV's English answers to a Hebrew word the projection does not carry and the packet records no variant unit in that slot at all, no textual decision has been taken for the alignment to honour and rule 9 forbids taking one here: align the English as printed against the token the projection does carry, on the terms the construction it stands in would otherwise take, and say in the unit's note that the English answers to a different reading of that word. `שֹׁפְטֵי צֶדֶק` → *the judges of the earth* keeps *of the earth* on `צֶדֶק` as the chain's rectum under rule 19, headed on *earth*, rather than marking the noun `unrepresented` and the English `added`. Rule 24's direction to head on the token most directly realizing the source head's lexeme is not defeated by this: where the divergence leaves no such token in the unit, head where the construction puts it, and name the divergence in the note under rule 8. An ASV marginal note reporting the other reading corroborates the divergence and decides nothing, by rule 38. Read the packet's variant lines before reaching for this paragraph, since a marked unit is what the sentences above govern, and do not read a lexical mismatch as licence to mark one side `unrepresented` and the other `added` where the pipeline has recorded no decision to record.
amendments.why: PRO.8.16 met a case rule 53 did not consider: the ASV translated אָרֶץ where the projection carries צֶדֶק, with no ketiv/qere or variant unit in the packet at all. Rule 53's existing text conditions its `added`/`unrepresented` marking on the packet marking the unit, and rule 9 forbids the aligner taking a textual decision, so the verse pass rightly aligned the English in place — but a later chapter reasoning by analogy from rule 53's shape would plausibly have marked it instead, since the rule never says what to do when nothing is marked. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule so that rule 53's over-broad reading is corrected where it stands; the added paragraph narrows scope and takes nothing away, and no corpus row contradicts it.

conventions: שֹׁפְטֵי צֶדֶק -> *the judges of the earth*: the ASV renders a Hebrew reading the projection does not carry, and the packet records no ketiv/qere or other variant unit in that slot. Rule 9 forbids taking a textual decision inside the alignment file, so *of the earth* stays on צֶדֶק as the chain's rectum under rule 19, headed on *earth*, rather than the noun being marked `unrepresented` and the English `added` on the analogy of rule 53. The divergence is named in the unit's note instead. Any later verse of this chapter meeting an unmarked divergence of the same kind is aligned the same way.

report: All 35 candidate lemma groups were read end to end. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently, with the source or the printed English licensing the difference; no cross-verse split was found, so patches is empty.

Preposition on a construct noun is uniform under rule 30's one-rendering test: fused at 8.3 (לְיַד -> Beside), 8.23 (מִקַּדְמֵי -> Before ... was), 8.25 (בְּטֶרֶם and לִפְנֵי -> Before), 8.28 (מִמָּעַל -> above) and 8.30 (לְפָנָיו -> before); split at 8.2, 8.3 (לְפִי -> at the entry), 8.20 and 8.27, where the ASV spends a separate word on the construct noun.

מִן is comparative *than* at 8.10 (*rather than*, headed on *than*), 8.11 and 8.19 (three times), ablative *from* at 8.23, and *of* at 8.22 and 8.35 — the ASV's own choice each time, always headed on the relational word.

The two לִי predicates in 8.14 are not a split: rule 49's closing paragraph fuses the one the ASV writes as a genitive (*is mine*), rule 43 gives the *have* to the other, and rule 49 itself draws that boundary by which English the ASV wrote.

Participles are routed by what stands in the Hebrew — article present to rule 41 (8.9 הַמֵּבִין -> *him that*), anarthrous substantival to rule 46 (8.9, 8.17, 8.21, 8.32, 8.35, 8.36), anarthrous attributive on a written noun to rule 41's articleless sentence (8.34) — and every one heads on the lexeme-bearing word.

יוֹם יוֹם -> *daily* is fused identically at 8.30 and 8.34, headed on the first occurrence. Rule 31's class-noun tie is resolved the same way twice (8.14 *sound knowledge*, 8.19 *fine gold*, both keeping the head on the class noun and both naming the alternative), against modifier-headed 8.2 *high places* and 8.6 *excellent things*.

Checked the added-versus-folded axis the candidate table is blind to. Supplied possessives are `added` at 8.12, 8.30 and 8.32 and are never folded; supplied connectives are `added` at 8.12, 8.16 and 8.18 while every waw-licensed connective is aligned; the one supplied object pronoun (8.33 *it*) is `added` while 8.36's *me* answers to a suffix. The single multi-word fold, עַד -> *While as yet* at 8.26, is a fixed temporal rendering of the preposition and not a stray connective, so it does not conflict with the added connectives.

BSB: the three disagreements are all לְ in 8.34 — the dative before *heareth me* (rule 40) and the two infinitive prepositions the ASV recasts as bare participles (rule 52). These are the documented convention difference, not errors, and no accepted edge was changed.

PRO.8.16 שֹׁפְטֵי צֶדֶק -> *the judges of the earth*: the ASV renders a Hebrew reading the projection does not carry, and the packet records no variant unit in that slot. Rule 53's marking regime is conditioned on the packet marking the unit and rule 9 forbids taking a textual decision in the alignment file, so *of the earth* rightly stays on צֶדֶק as the chain's rectum. Recorded as a convention and returned as an amendment to rule 53, which is where the gap is.
